nodes.label: Graphify-First Directive
nodes.rationale: Ensures the installed graphify skill/instructions are consulted before doing anything else whenever the user types /graphify.

nodes.label: Provider Adapter Pattern
nodes.rationale: One provider per file; adding a provider must not require editing providerManager.ts beyond one registration entry, keeping the manager a thin registry.

nodes.label: Normalize At Adapter Boundary
nodes.rationale: The provider returns the shared shape from docs/contracts.md so nothing downstream needs to know which vendor answered.

nodes.label: No API Key In Code Rule
nodes.rationale: Keys come from settings only - never code, defaults, tests, fixtures, or comments - and are sent to exactly one endpoint: the selected provider's.
nodes.norm_label: no api key in code rule
nodes.community_name: No API Key In Code Rule

nodes.label: Provider Text Output Validation
nodes.rationale: processText JSON must be fence-stripped, parsed inside try/catch, and field-validated before use - never trust a language model's JSON blindly or return a half-filled object on failure.

nodes.label: AnkiConnectClient
nodes.rationale: Single typed wrapper for all AnkiConnect traffic; the URL is passed in at construction rather than read from this.settings inside a standalone function, so the client isn't coupled to the plugin instance.

nodes.label: Idempotent Sync Rule
nodes.rationale: No anki_note_id -> addNote then write the ID back; has an ID -> updateNoteFields, never create; AnkiConnect reports the note missing -> clear the ID then addNote; re-running sync on an unchanged note must be a no-op, never a duplicate.

nodes.label: Heading-Based Content Parsing
nodes.rationale: A section runs from its heading to the next heading of the same or higher level, or EOF; alternative schemes (YAML in body, custom delimiters, HTML comments) require a design-doc change before a code change.

nodes.label: Media Filename Format
nodes.rationale: Default prefix _obsidian_ is what stops Anki's Check Media from deleting plugin files; the word component comes from user content and must be sanitized (strip path separators/control chars, truncate) while still allowing Unicode.

nodes.label: Content Update Append Rule
nodes.rationale: Adding audio/image appends into the matching ## Section rather than rewriting the whole file, preserving everything else byte for byte.

nodes.label: Sync Error Path Coverage
nodes.rationale: Every case (AnkiConnect offline, note not found, duplicate note, parse error, model not found) needs an explicit branch and a user-facing Notice; a silent catch {} is never acceptable.

nodes.label: Copy Style Rules
nodes.rationale: All user-facing strings in English for the Obsidian community store; sentence case; bold for literal UI labels; arrow notation for navigation; reuse the existing emoji set instead of inventing icons; failure copy states what happened and what to do next.

nodes.label: Long Operation Feedback
nodes.rationale: AI calls take 5-30s; a persistent Notice that updates as work progresses, replaced by a success toast, is required - a static Processing... with no updates is a bug.

nodes.label: Themed Styling Rule
nodes.rationale: Use Obsidian CSS variables, never hardcoded hex, so the plugin looks correct in light/dark/community themes; prefix CSS classes to avoid collisions with other plugins.

nodes.label: Shared Settings State Rule
nodes.rationale: Settings tab and sidebar view must read and write the same this.settings object and both re-render on change; two copies drifting apart is called out as the single most likely bug in this area.

nodes.label: Listener Cleanup Rule
nodes.rationale: Every listener from a view or modal uses registerDomEvent/registerEvent/registerInterval, or is torn down in onClose; detached listeners survive plugin reload and cause duplicate handlers.

nodes.label: Add Provider Pre-Check
nodes.rationale: Determine the task (text/audio/image) and cloud-vs-local before writing code; if a vendor's response shape doesn't fit the normalized output, stop and ask rather than unilaterally widening the shared interface.

nodes.label: Graphify Query Fast Path
nodes.rationale: If graphify-out/graph.json already exists and the request is a natural-language question rather than an explicit rebuild command, skip Steps 1-5 entirely and jump straight to query - the graph is already built.

nodes.label: AST vs Semantic Extraction Split
nodes.rationale: Code is extracted structurally via AST with no LLM or API key needed; semantic extraction for docs/papers/images uses Gemini only if a key is already set, otherwise the host agent itself is the LLM. graphify never reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY, so a code-only corpus skips semantic extraction entirely and needs no key.

nodes.label: Semantic Extraction Cache (Step B0)
nodes.rationale: Cache entries are keyed to the extraction prompt file (SPEC_PATH) so a prompt upgrade re-extracts affected files instead of replaying stale results, while unchanged prompts keep their cached entries (#1939).

nodes.label: Parallel Subagent Dispatch (Steps B1-B3)
nodes.rationale: All chunk subagents must be dispatched in a single message with subagent_type=general-purpose, never Explore (which is read-only and cannot write chunk files, silently dropping results); real token counts are read from the Agent tool's usage field and patched into each chunk JSON before merging since the chunk JSON's own token fields are placeholder zeros.

nodes.label: Graph Shrink Guard (#479)
nodes.rationale: to_json() refuses to write a new graph.json that is smaller than the existing one, so an empty or bad extraction can't silently clobber a good graph; overriding an intentional shrink requires --force.

nodes.label: Manifest Stamping Rule (#2015/#1948)
nodes.rationale: Only semantic files that actually produced output this run get stamped in the manifest; a changed file whose chunk failed or was omitted must stay unstamped, or have its stale semantic_hash cleared, so the next --update re-queues it instead of losing its content forever.

nodes.label: Graphify Honesty Rules
nodes.rationale: Never invent an edge (use AMBIGUOUS instead), never skip the corpus-size warning, always show token cost, never hide cohesion scores behind symbols, never run HTML viz above 5000 nodes without warning.

nodes.label: Post-Pipeline Guide Behavior
nodes.rationale: After the pipeline finishes, pick the single most interesting suggested question - the one crossing the most community boundaries - and offer to trace it; the graph is the map, and the skill's job afterward is to be the guide, ending each answer with a follow-up so exploration continues.

nodes.label: --watch Background Watcher
nodes.rationale: Code-only changes trigger an immediate AST rebuild with no LLM needed; doc/paper/image changes only write a needs_update flag because they require LLM semantic re-extraction; a 3s debounce absorbs a burst of parallel agent writes so a wave of edits doesn't trigger one rebuild per file.

nodes.label: Neo4j / FalkorDB Export
nodes.rationale: Both use MERGE so re-running never creates duplicates; FalkorDB's GRAPH.QUERY runs one statement at a time (no bulk cypher-shell import like Neo4j), so --falkordb-push is preferred over the raw cypher.txt for loading.

nodes.label: Graphify MCP Server
nodes.rationale: Exposes query_graph/get_node/get_neighbors/get_community/god_nodes/graph_stats/shortest_path over stdio; Claude Desktop can't run $(...) and uv-tool installs mean system python3 can't import graphify, so its config must use the absolute interpreter path from .graphify_python.

nodes.label: Token Reduction Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Only runs when total_words exceeds 5000 - for small corpora the graph's value is structural clarity, not token compression.

nodes.label: Node ID Format Rule
nodes.rationale: IDs must be {full-repo-relative-stem}_{entity} using every directory level, matching exactly what the AST extractor generates, so semantic and AST nodes for the same entity dedupe instead of creating orphan ghost-duplicates; chunk-number suffixes are never appended.

nodes.label: Confidence Score Rubric
nodes.rationale: Discrete values (0.95/0.85/0.75/0.65/0.55) are required for INFERRED edges instead of a continuous range, because production data showed models collapsing continuous guidance into a 0.5/0.85+ bimodal split; anything not matching the ladder should be AMBIGUOUS rather than a low float.

nodes.label: Semantic Similarity Edge Guidance
nodes.rationale: semantically_similar_to edges are only for genuinely non-obvious, cross-cutting similarity (e.g. two validators that never call each other), scored 0.6-0.95 - not for trivially similar things.

nodes.label: Hyperedge Usage Guidance
nodes.rationale: Hyperedges are for 3+ nodes participating together in a pattern not captured by pairwise edges (e.g. all classes implementing a common protocol); capped at 3 per chunk to avoid overuse.

nodes.label: Calls Edge Direction & Language-Purity Rule
nodes.rationale: calls edges must point caller to callee, never reversed, and must stay within a single language - a Python function can never `calls` a JS/TS/Go/Rust/Java symbol.

nodes.label: GitHub Clone & Cross-Repo Merge
nodes.rationale: Clones into ~/.graphify/repos/<owner>/<repo> and reuses existing clones on repeat runs; merge-graphs tags each node in the merged graph with a repo attribute so results can be filtered by origin.

nodes.label: Monorepo Multi-Subfolder Merge
nodes.rationale: Running the skill pipeline separately on each subfolder would clobber the same graphify-out/ directory, so each subfolder is extracted via the CLI directly (which places graphify-out/ inside the scanned path) and merged afterward with merge-graphs at the project root.

nodes.label: Post-Commit Auto-Rebuild Hook
nodes.rationale: Triggers once per commit, detects changed code files via git diff HEAD~1 and re-runs AST extraction only; doc/image changes are ignored by the hook and need a manual /graphify --update; it appends to an existing post-commit hook rather than replacing it.

nodes.label: Native CLAUDE.md Integration
nodes.rationale: graphify claude install writes a ## graphify section into the project's CLAUDE.md instructing Claude to check the graph before answering codebase questions and rebuild it after code changes, so no manual /graphify invocation is needed in future sessions.

nodes.label: Constrained Query Expansion (Step 0)
nodes.rationale: graphify query matches via case-folded substring plus IDF with no stemming, synonyms, or cross-language matching, so a wording mismatch between the question and the graph's own vocabulary collapses the answer to noise unless the question is expanded first using only tokens actually present in the graph's label vocabulary - never invented tokens.

nodes.label: save-result Feedback Loop
nodes.rationale: Answers are saved back into the graph via save-result with --outcome useful/dead_end/corrected so a later --update extracts the Q&A as a node, and future sessions read preferred sources and avoid dead ends via LESSONS.md - a self-improving loop.

nodes.label: Self-Composed Whisper Prompt
nodes.rationale: Rather than a separate API call, the host model writes its own one-sentence domain hint from the corpus's god-node labels and passes it as Whisper's initial_prompt to improve accuracy on domain vocabulary; falls back to a generic punctuation-only prompt when the corpus is video-only.

nodes.label: Incremental --update Flow
nodes.rationale: detect_incremental finds new/changed/deleted files since the last run; if every changed file is code, semantic extraction is skipped entirely since no LLM is needed.

nodes.label: build_merge Direct Graph Read
nodes.rationale: build_merge() reads graph.json directly instead of round-tripping through NetworkX so edge direction (calls/implements/imports) is always preserved (#801); prune_sources is only for genuinely deleted files since changed files are reconciled by replace-on-re-extract (#1344), and root= keeps prune paths relativized to the same base as the freshly merged nodes.

nodes.label: --cluster-only Self-Contained Rerun
nodes.rationale: cluster-only re-clusters, names communities, and regenerates GRAPH_REPORT.md/graph.json/graph.html from the existing graph by itself; Steps 5-9 must not be re-run afterward because they read intermediate files that a prior build's cleanup already deleted (#1392).

nodes.label: Obsidian Plugin Release CI
nodes.rationale: Optional styles.css is handled via a conditional step (styles.outputs.exists) so plugins without a stylesheet don't fail attestation or the release step by referencing a missing file.
